summary: The release supply chain now has enforced human review, strict CI gating, pre-publication SPDX SBOM generation, immutable releases with native release attestations, and continuous OpenSSF Scorecard analysis. All actionable findings from this review were remediated.

findings.title: Release credential workflows could merge without human approval
findings.evidence: The live Protect main ruleset previously required zero approvals.
findings.resolution: The ruleset now requires one fresh code-owner approval, dismisses stale approvals, requires approval from someone other than the last pusher, requires resolved review threads, uses strict required checks, and retains no bypass actors.

findings.title: Published release tags and assets were mutable
findings.evidence: The repository immutable-release endpoint was not enabled.
findings.resolution: Immutable releases are enabled. Future release tags and assets are locked after publication and GitHub generates a cryptographic release attestation.

findings.title: No continuous OpenSSF Scorecard assessment
findings.resolution: Added a SHA-pinned, OIDC-publishing Scorecard workflow with SARIF artifact retention and code-scanning upload, plus executable validation and negative regression tests.

findings.title: Published releases lacked a distributable SPDX SBOM
findings.evidence: Immutable publication previously occurred without a repository-specific SBOM asset.
findings.resolution: Release-please now creates a draft and version tag. A tag-triggered workflow generates an SPDX 2.3 SBOM under read-only permissions, validates source and exact runtime package metadata, transfers only the validated artifact into a contents-write job, checksum-verifies the uploaded asset, and publishes the immutable release.

residuals.reason: GitHub immutable releases provide a cryptographic release attestation for the tag, commit, and assets. A higher SLSA Build level becomes relevant when the project introduces a separate build artifact.
